## What is monitored

Line Increase is monitored as three things: the **model's ranking**, the **offered cohort**
and what it goes on to do, and the **settings** that shape the funnel. Each new scoring of the
book is out-of-sample for accounts booked after training, unlike most of the development book.
Outcomes — the label, deterioration and default — are read once they mature. The thresholds
are policy constants (`wiki/facts/policy.py`) and the model's own gates. Events, for the
calibration floor, are positives of `{{< var li.target >}}` unless the row says otherwise.

| Metric | Population | Threshold | Frequency | Action on breach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AUC | new accounts with matured outcomes | below the gate, {{< var li.gate.auc_min >}} | when outcomes mature | One cohort below: review with the validator, reading the interval. Two consecutive: redevelopment ([8.9](gate.qmd)). |
| Top-quintile lift, and the best single input's lift | the same | the model's lift below {{< var li.gate.lift_min >}}×, or not above the best single input's | when outcomes mature | Below the gate: as AUC. Not above the best input: review whether the model earns its place (finding 3). |
| Observed / predicted label rate among offers | offers with matured outcomes, out-of-sample only | outside {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}} to {{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}, on at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} positives | when outcomes mature | Below the floor: record and watch. At or above it: count toward trigger 3. |
| Deterioration and default rate among offers, against the book's | offers with matured outcomes | above the book's rate, on at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} events of that kind, with an exact binomial test | when outcomes mature | Review with the credit policy owner (proposed; to be named): this is the outcome no gate measures (finding 1). |
| Offer share and count | every scoring of the book | the share above the threshold moving away from {{< var li.thr.share_book >}} by more than {{< var monitoring.rule_hit_move >}} of it | every scoring run | Check the inputs before the threshold (finding 2). |
| Funnel by clause | every scoring of the book | any clause's count moving by more than {{< var monitoring.rule_hit_move >}} of its development value | every scoring run | Report to the credit policy owner; a moved clause is a policy change in effect. |
| Binding cap counts | accounts with an amount | any cap that binds on no account | every scoring run | Report as an untested control, as for a dead trigger clause in D7. |
| Offers on the Early Warning screen | offers | share High or Medium, and share with a trigger other than the utilisation rules, against the book's | every scoring run | Above the book's on either: review with the Early Warning owner before offers go out ([8.7](limitations.qmd#li-observations)). |
| Committed amount and assumed exposure | offers | reported, not thresholded | every scoring run | Size limits and capital on the committed amount (finding 5). |
| Threshold and PD ceiling at a retrain | the retrained model | any change | every retrain | The share was held and the level moved: the policy owner signs off the new values before use ([8.4](assumptions.qmd#li-shares)). |
| Unread configuration | `LINE_INCREASE` | any key no code reads | every `verify.py` run | Report (finding 4). |
| Candidates list: share of training rows | the list served | reported, not thresholded | every scoring run | Any training row on the list makes its hit rate in-sample (finding 2). |

The deterioration and default row is the control finding 1 needs until a gate measures the
cohort; the offers-on-EWS row is the observation's control. The first reading of the label
rate on offers that were actually made will also be the first evidence of what the label
means on a real book (finding 6).

| AUC | {{< var li.auc >}} (interval {{< var li.boot.auc.lo >}}–{{< var li.boot.auc.hi >}}) | held-out accounts |
| Top-quintile lift | {{< var li.lift >}}× (interval {{< var li.boot.lift.lo >}}×–{{< var li.boot.lift.hi >}}×) | held-out accounts |

| Offers High or Medium on Early Warning; with a non-utilisation trigger | {{< var li.offers.ews.high_or_medium.share >}}; {{< var li.offers.ews.non_util_trigger.share >}} (book {{< var li.book.ews.high_or_medium.share >}}; {{< var li.book.ews.non_util_trigger.share >}}) | offers and the book |

## Redevelopment triggers {#li-redevelopment-triggers}

Any one of these starts a redevelopment, with the validator informed:

1. AUC or lift below its gate in two consecutive cohorts with matured outcomes.
2. The model's lift not above the best single input's in two consecutive cohorts (finding 3).
3. Observed / predicted among offers outside the tolerance in two consecutive cohorts, each
   with at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} positives behind it. Below that count
   a breach is recorded and watched, not acted on.
4. A change to any input's definition or source — including any change to the scorecard,
   which supplies the PD three times over ([8.2](data.qmd#li-score-input)), and to `MARKET`,
   whose hurdle decides the fourth clause.

A change to any value in `LINE_INCREASE` goes to the credit policy owner (proposed; to be
named) rather than to redevelopment, after which [8.5](performance.qmd) and
[8.6](sensitivity.qmd) are re-run.

A redevelopment is where the open findings are acted on: cohort gates that can fail
(finding 1), an out-of-fold threshold (finding 2), a lift gate against the best single input
(finding 3), a measured drawdown (finding 5) and a defined label (finding 6). Every
redevelopment re-runs [8.5](performance.qmd) and passes the gate.

## What is automated today

This plan is documented, not yet automated. The platform has one booked book and one draw of
outcomes, so there is no new cohort to compare. What runs today is the development side:
`python verify.py` recomputes the held-out AUC and lift and the cohort gates against its own
copies of the gates ([8.9](gate.qmd)), and on `main` recomputes every fact on these pages —
the funnel, the caps, the cohort's outcomes and Early Warning flags, the baselines, the unread
configuration key — from the committed model and data on every run
([D9](../d9-implementation.qmd)).
